steps:
WARNING: this deletes the project file. Do it in a scratch folder made for this, <S> below (for example C:\Scratch\sourcepath-test), holding nothing but the unzipped project.
1. Unzip export-path-sourcepath-as-path.zip into <S>, so that <S>\export-path-sourcepath-as-path.twinproj is the only file there. Open it in the twinBASIC IDE. Export Verbose is on.
2. Project Settings > Export > Export Path: type ${SourcePath}. The editor refuses it: "${SourcePath} on it's own is not allowed. This would DELETE the project file ...".
3. Type <S> in full instead (C:\Scratch\sourcepath-test). The editor accepts it. Apply.
4. Choose File > Export Project.
5. See, in the DEBUG CONSOLE, [EXPORT]  DELETED: \\?\<S>\export-path-sourcepath-as-path.twinproj, and then [EXPORT] COMPLETED. The project file is no longer on disk; the project is still open, and Save Project would write it back.
Re-measured on BETA 995 by `ide-test.bat --only export`, which calls exportProjectTo() on the project's own folder (the compiler's side: step 4 and 5). Step 3, that the Settings editor accepts the full path, is read from the validate() function of project.exportPath in ide/main.js, which compares the text with ${sourcepath} and ${sourcepath}\ and does not resolve the path; it has not been tried by hand.
